THEME: CYBER NEON METROPOLIS. A rain-slick futuristic megacity at night seen as a stylised map-like top-down illustration: glowing cyan and hot-magenta neon, deep violet and midnight-black lacquer, chrome circuit traces. Upper half: a dense skyline crown along the top arch, holo billboards (pictograms only), flying traffic light trails that sweep along the ramp lanes, a hexagonal data-core plaza with radiating circuit streets around the central hole, glowing ring plazas under the three bumpers. Middle: neon boulevards converging toward the centre, circuit-board city blocks. Lower third: a retro-futuristic sunset grid horizon fading into dark asphalt with faint wet reflections and thin neon lane lines running toward the flippers.
ASSET: one flat, full-bleed pinball PLAYFIELD PRINT, the painted artwork that is silk-screened onto the wooden playfield of a pinball machine. Tall portrait image, aspect ratio exactly 1:2 (width : height), top of the table at the top of the image. Opaque, no transparency.

THE ATTACHED IMAGE IS A LAYOUT MAP, NOT ART. It shows, in flat diagram colours, where real 3D hardware will later be mounted ON TOP of your painting. Never reproduce its colours, lines or shapes. Use it only to compose the painting so the artwork fits the machine:
- grey-blue area inside the brown arch = the playfield surface you paint. The black corners outside the arch stay plain black.
- yellow discs = pop bumpers. Paint a decorative circular motif centred under each one (it will peek out around the bumper body).
- black disc with white ring = a hole the ball falls into. Paint an ornamental ring or portal around it.
- large light-grey disc = a tall toy stands here. Paint a base plate or plaza for it.
- green translucent ribbons = ramps that pass ABOVE the playfield. The painting continues underneath them. Where a green ribbon begins in the middle of the table (its lower end), paint an inviting lane or arrow-like flow leading into it.
- thin white outlines (circles, squares, arrows, stars, shields) = lamp inserts that the game draws itself. Keep the painting calm, darker and low-contrast right there, and let surrounding ornaments frame these groups instead of crossing them.
- pink short bars = targets, blue lines = clear plastic walls, light grey lines = metal guides, red triangles = slingshots, orange bars = flippers, brown = wooden rails. Do not paint these objects. Paint flowing ornamental borders that run along them.
- the dark vertical strip at the far right = the ball shooter lane. Paint it as a dark lane with a subtle repeating chevron pattern pointing up.
- the bottom dark band = hidden under the apron: plain dark.

HARD RULES: completely flat 2D print seen exactly from straight above (orthographic). The two smaller purple dashed circles in the middle are gravity wells: paint one swirling red-orange planet vortex (left) and one ringed golden planet vortex (right), each exactly centred in its circle, with fine spiral star dust. Lower third: dark mahogany and midnight-blue enamel with delicate brass filigree, thin engraved orbit arcs and a few small stars, calm and elegant.

THE ATTACHED IMAGE IS A CUTTING TEMPLATE: seven white shapes on black. Reproduce the sheet with every white shape replaced by one finished printed piece that has exactly the same outline, position and size as the white shape. THE SEVEN PIECES:
1. Tall triangle (top left) = slingshot plastic. A bold vertical illustration that fills the whole triangle, with its focal subject in the wide upper-left part.
2. Bent strip like a hockey stick (top centre) = lane guide plastic. A continuous ornamental pattern that runs along the strip.
3. Shape with a concave curved edge (top right) = back-corner panel. A richly illustrated scene that fills the whole piece.
4. Disc (right, below the corner) = pop bumper cap seen from straight above. A radial emblem with a clear centre, concentric rings and a bright rim.
5. Upper rounded rectangle = sign plate with three bold chevron arrows pointing up, glowing.
6. Lower rounded rectangle = sign plate with one pictogram icon in the middle and decorative end caps.
7. Large oval (bottom) = apron badge: the emblem of this pinball machine as a pure picture emblem.

LOOK OF EVERY PIECE: completely flat 2D print seen exactly from straight above, artwork running edge to edge inside its outline, a thin dark keyline along the outline and a fine bright bevel line just inside it like polished cut acrylic.
